study ('study number') never repeats, one standardized mean difference yi with vi per study and weeks a covariate; Pellegrini & Hicks (1972) give an aware and a blind tester row under one author label, the table rabe_hesketh's expectancy.dta holds and was read flat, and rma puts the study effect on single rows.

TP of n1 (diseased) and TN of n2 (non-diseased), with FN and FP their complements, are each study's two reference groups as columns; metaprop pools TP of n1 and TN of n2 and metabin(TP, n1, n2-TN, n2) treats the groups as arms, so the counts stack into the study x group long form, as dat.kearon1998's, and SampleID repeats for one sample.

Ne, Me, Se (nedocromil) and Nc, Mc, Sc (placebo) are the size, mean and SD of the maximum FEV1 fall in each trial's two arms, arm summaries as HSAUR3 toothpaste's; metacont by agegroup pools one difference per trial, and author labels recur only for distinct trials (DeBenedictis 1994a, 1994b, 1995).
One log hazard ratio lnHR with selnHR per trial ('4 trials'), author never repeating; metagen's common-effect model pools single rows.

ai of n1i and ci of n2i are each trial's deaths or reinfarctions in its two arms as columns, one row per trial and outcome table (6, 9, 10, 11, 12a, 12b); binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, id ('trial id number') also repeats across the outcome tables of the long-term trials, rma.peto pools each table, and metadat holds no long form.

study_id ('unique id for study') and es_id are both unique over the rows, so no column indexes the '62 studies' the description names, and the effect sizes yi with vi enter an ordinary random-effects meta-analysis (hand check #162); population, task and stimulation are effect covariates.

factual and conceptual are each participant's memory scores on the two question types of one quiz as columns ('There were two types of questions, factual and conceptual questions'), overall their mean, one row per pid; talk ('TED talk seen by participant', five levels) is between participants, and Singmann's case study (stats_for_experiments, ch. 6) fits aov_car(conceptual ~ condition + Error(pid), laptop_urry), so no model stacks the scores and afex holds no long form.

COH01 to COH05 are each soldier's five cohesion items as columns, a person by item structure stored wide (carData DavisThin), with no soldier id; PLATOON ('Lower-level Platoon Identifier') holds a few soldiers each in 'four platoons further nested within two larger units', too few for a grouping factor the source does not fit, and the tutorial only demonstrates data manipulation.

One observer's detection trials, one row per trial with Contrast ('6 luminance contrast levels' and catch trials) and Stim fixed; Rating is the confidence rating, the response, and no column indexes a session or block.

One observer's '16 sessions of 224 trials', stored as the 32 noise samples N of each trial over time; the rows repeat within trials and sessions, but no column indexes either (datasets rock's unindexed cores), and MPDiR ch. 6 estimates the classification image by lm(N ~ time/resp - 1) without a random effect.

One observer's 2AFC trials from 'two randomly interleaved staircases'; StairCase has two levels, a design factor, and Trial ('the trial number for the staircase') numbers each staircase's own trials, so equal Trial values are different trials; MPDiR ch. 5 fits glm(Response ~ log10(Contrast), binomial(mafc.logit(2))).

One observer's counts NumUpward and NumDownward per cell of Phaseshift, WaveForm, TempFreq and Direction, fixed design factors; MPDiR ch. 4 fits glm(cbind(NumUpward, NumDownward) ~ Direction * WaveForm * TempFreq * Phaseshift, binomial) with several links, and no column indexes a unit.

fall_k, spring_k and spring_g1 are each student's reading scores in fall kindergarten, spring kindergarten and spring first grade as columns ('Wide dataset to be used for growth modeling'), studentid unique; MLMusingR holds no long form.

One row per day of one Capital Bikeshare series ('500 daily observations'); year, month, day_of_week and weekend are calendar indices, not units (datasets airquality, bambi_bikes), and Bayes Rules! fits rides by stan_glm without grouping.
One row per person; group classifies the 75 people into control and football players without and with concussion history, years counts the years played, and nothing repeats within a unit.

country ('country of origin') indexes the nationalities the artists repeat within, most holding several, as HSAUR3 Forbes2000's country holds its companies, while gender and department classify; Bayes Rules! (ch. 8) fits a Beta-Binomial of genx on moma_sample, a random sample of these artists, with no grouping. artist also repeats over departments with every other column constant, copies of one artist rather than repeated measures.

Daily weather at 'three Australian cities: Wollongong, Hobart, and Uluru', location a design factor of three levels; year, month and day_of_year are calendar indices of sampled days, not units, and Bayes Rules! enters location as a fixed predictor (chapter 11, on weather_WU).

y8 to y36 are each rat's weights on days 8, 15, 22, 29 and 36 as columns ('measured weekly over 5 weeks'), rat unique, and the page fits runMLwiN(c(y8, y15, y22, y29, y36) ~ 1 + (1 | rat), D = 'Multivariate Normal'); these are Gelfand et al.'s (1990) rats, whose long form posteriordb's rats_data.json.zip holds in the registry.
'Twenty rats were randomly assigned to a control condition or three doses of fluoxetine', one row per rat; dose is a fixed design factor, time.immob the response, and no column indexes a unit.
Number is the ball ("the integers from 1 to 39, representing the numbered balls"), one row each, and Frequency its count over the 122 weekly draws; no unit repeats and the page fits no model.

One row per country and year of two annual series: Country (Australia, NewZealand) is a two-level design factor, Year the series' time index with one row per country, and Beer, Wine and Spirit three different beverages; the page only plots xyplot(Beer+Wine+Spirit ~ Year | Country).
POP1992 to POP1996 are each city's population ("in 1000's for 1992" to 1996) as columns, one row per CITY; REGION is a five-level location attribute.

census1886 and survey1889 are each worker category's number of workers by two investigations ("Numbers of workers in each of 14 different categories" in the 1886 census and the 1889 survey) as columns, one row per category, as HSAUR3 waves' two methods; avwage is the survey's alone.

One row per cricketer; year is the birth year, which the page's coxph(Surv(life, kia) ~ bs(year,3) + left) fits as a spline covariate, and dead, acd, kia and inbed are each cricketer's event indicators; no unit repeats.

One row per country and year of two annual series: Country (Australia, NewZealand) is a two-level design factor, Year the series' time index with one row per country, and Beer, Wine and Spirit three different beverages; the page only plots xyplot(Beer+Wine+Spirit ~ Year | Country).

id indexes four athletes ("four out of the 25 applicants"), several power levels each, but four levels fall under the five-level rule and the page fits lm(o2 ~ id + wattsPerKg:id), each athlete's line fixed; the book's random coefficients model is humanpower1's.
One row per named hurricane (Name); Year is its landfall year, most years holding one hurricane, a time covariate and no wave, and the page plots log(deaths+0.5) on log(NDAM2014) with no model.

chemical and magnetic are each slag sample's iron content by the two methods ("Two methods for measuring the iron content in samples of slag were compared") as columns, one row per sample, as pingouin blandaltman; the page fits lm(chemical ~ magnetic).

BC, Alberta, Prairies, Ontario, Quebec and Atlantic are one measure, the "monthly labour force counts" of six regions, as columns, one row per month (Date); the long form is month x region, as agridat hazell.vegetables' crops.
One row per family ("33 families randomly sampled from a community of 600 families"), familysize a count of members and expenses the weekly cost; no unit repeats and the page fits no model.

One row per man of the NSW experiment with his real earnings in 1974 and 1975 beside the 1978 outcome: a baseline-outcome pair, as ros chile, since the documented analyses regress re78 on trt with the earlier years as covariates; trt is the treatment, and no column indexes a unit the rows repeat within.

race holds one Distance per event (Distance constant within each of the 9 races), so it restates the covariate: the standard events are a design factor, and the page fits lm(log(Time) ~ log(Distance)) without them; year dates each record (hand check #162).

One row per plant; Block has two levels, under five, fitted fixed in aov(ShootDryMass ~ Block + variety * fert) (Maindonald and Braun 2010, sec. 7.2.1), and PlantNo numbers the twelve plants of each treatment, so a number's six rows are six plants of six treatments.

One row per survey respondent; country (australia, other), gender and the other factors are respondent attributes of few levels, and the page regresses BDI on principal components of the support scores; no unit repeats.

One row per record distance (Distance, road or track); Place is the venue of a record, most venues holding one, and Date its day, so no unit repeats; the page plots log(Time) on log(Distance) by roadORtrack.

One row per surveyed respondent ("reported frequency of visits to national parks"), with no park-site column; income and travel are categorical attributes beside their dummies, and the page fits glm(anvisits ~ gender + factor(income) + factor(travel), family=poisson) and glm.nb.
One row per passenger; class (four levels), age and sex are fixed attributes, and the page fits glm(survival ~ age + sex + factor(class), family=binomial); no unit repeats.

Field has three levels, under five, the survey's explanatory factor fitted fixed in glm(AphidCount ~ Field, family = poisson()); Sample numbers the 15 sample points within each field, one row each, and ID is the row id.

DSample is the "Experimental unit identifier, representing the replicate number", one row each, of a completely randomized 2 x 3 x 2 factorial fitted as lm(C ~ Size * Weight * Time); Time is a two-level shaking-time treatment.

Run has two levels ("each time period and source combination is repeated in two separate runs"), fitted fixed in glm(Conidia ~ Run + (log(Time) + Period) * Source, family = poisson()), under five; DUnit numbers the units within a run, one row each, and Time is the exposure duration.

Rep is the block of "two blocks corresponding to separate experimental occasions", fitted fixed in lm(log(Km) ~ Rep + Voltage), under five; DUnit is one measurement per voltage and block, so no unit repeats.
Site has four levels (C, L, P, W), fitted fixed with its own slopes in lm(log10(TotalSeed) ~ Site * (HLength + Spikelets)), under five; Sample is the unique sample point.

id is one marriage whose single survival time MLMUS4 sec. 15.6 (ch15.do) splits at each birth (numkids rises within id, lower and upper constant, at most one divorce, on the last row), fitted by a single-level lognormal AFT model (streg ... numkids, distribution(lognormal)); a split-episode layout is no cluster (outside check).

id indexes three patients (A, B, C) whose recurrent events MLMUS4 sec. 15.12 (ch15.do) lists to show the total-time, counting-process and gap-time layouts, fitting no model; three levels fall under the five-level rule.

like_AB and like_BA (and dislike_AB, dislike_BA) are each dyad's two directions as columns, one row per pair of 18 monks, which McElreath's 2022 course (week 8) models with correlated dyad effects; the wide rule holds although the monks A and B repeat across rows (outside check).

giftsAB and giftsBA are each dyad's two directions as columns, one row per pair of 25 households (hidA, hidB), which McElreath's m14.7 (R code 14.31) models with correlated giving and receiving effects per household and correlated dyad effects; the wide rule holds although the households repeat (outside check).

id is unique, one New York City listing per row, with no host or neighborhood column; host_since and days date the listing's host, and BeyondMLR ch. 4 open-ended exercise 1 asks for a model of number_of_reviews; no unit repeats.

One row per bill one waitress served; Day (the seven weekdays) and Meal (Lunch, Dinner, Late Night) are exhaustive design classifications, not sampled units, and BeyondMLR ch. 1 open-ended exercise 2 asks for a regression of the tip.

One row per college or university; region holds six exhaustive U.S. regions (C, MW, NE, SE, SW, W), a design factor, as BeyondMLR ch. 4's campus crime case study fits region fixed on c_data.csv, and type (U, C) two levels; ch. 6 open-ended exercise 2 models the violent share of crimes.

state indexes the U.S. state the universities repeat within, 20 states of 1 to 8 universities each (median 1.5; TX 8, OH 6, MI 5, NC 4), an area factor of many levels sampled from the U.S. states, as HSAUR3 Forbes2000's country; BeyondMLR ch. 4 guided exercise 5 fits single-level Poisson regressions of burg09 and no source fits state; re-filed with state.

MathAvgScore.0 to MathAvgScore.2 are each Minnesota school's mean MCA-II math score in 2008, 2009 and 2010 as columns, one row per school (schoolid); the BeyondMLR ch. 9 case study gathers them into a long table and fits lmer(MathAvgScore ~ year08 + (year08|schoolid)) there.
One row per camping party; persons and child count its members and camper is binary, and BeyondMLR ch. 4 open-ended exercise 4 asks for a model of the fish caught (count); no unit repeats.

One row per house sale, with no house id or zip code; date counts the sale's day, many sales per day, a time covariate and no surveyed unit, and BeyondMLR ch. 1 guided exercise 3 fits linear regressions of price or log price on sqft.

hgt13, hgt18, hgt23 and hgt28 are each plant's height on four days as columns, which BeyondMLR ch. 10 gathers into a long table; the wide rule holds although pot groups the plants of ch. 11's germination exercise (hand check #162).

One row per strike begun in June of a year 1968-1976 ('Greene (2003) only provides the June data for each year'); uoutput ('unanticipated output') takes one value per year, which no column holds, a stand-in and no id, and the page fits survreg(Surv(duration) ~ uoutput, dist = 'weibull') (Greene 2003, Example 22.10).

One row per household (idcase, 'a cross-section' of 'households') with one choice of heating system, depvar; the five alternatives' costs ic.*, oc.* and pb.* are attributes of that one choice rather than repeated measures, and region has four levels, a design factor; a single-level choice model, as its copy pymc_examples heating_data_r.csv was read.

One row per contract strike, 1968-1976 (Kennan 1985; 'a cross-section'); gdp, the 'deviation of monthly log industrial production' in the strike's month, takes one value per month, which no column holds, a stand-in and no id, and Cameron and Trivedi (2005, pp. 574-5 and 582) fit duration models of dur.

agriculture, industry, construction, transport and commerce are one measure, the 'Real national income' index (1952 = 100), of five sectors as columns ('An annual multiple time series from 1952 to 1988'), one row per year, so the long form is year x sector, as agridat hazell.vegetables' crops; the example only plots it, and no registry object or frame table holds the long form.

tv and radio are one measure, the 'advertising expenditures (in real terms)', of two media as columns ('A four-weekly multiple time series from 1978(1) to 1994(13)'), one row per four-week period, so the long form is period x medium, as DAAG jobs' regions; the examples compute the extended autocorrelation function of log(tv) and fit no model across the media.

gold and silver are one measure, the 'spot price', of two metals as columns ('A daily multiple time series from 1977-12-30 to 2012-12-31'), one row per day, so the long form is day x metal, as DAAG jobs' regions; the examples fit an ARFIMA model to the absolute gold returns and a VAR(2) to the two monthly log prices, no random effect.

capitalcost, laborcost, energycost and materialscost ('cost share') and capitalprice, laborprice, energyprice and materialsprice ('price') are two measures of four inputs as columns beside the cost index ('An annual multiple time series from 1947 to 1971'), one row per year, so the long form is year x input, as zuur_mixed Antarcticbirds' species; the example only plots it.

black and white are one measure, the 'average monthly European spot prices' in US dollars per ton, of two peppers as columns ('A monthly multiple time series from 1973(10) to 1996(4)'), one row per month, so the long form is month x pepper, as DAAG jobs' regions; the examples run unit-root tests on the white price and cointegration tests on both, no random effect.

One row per OCC1950 occupation code and 'one column for each year' of IPUMS-US, 1850 to 2016, each the occupation's share of the population, so the occupation is the unit stored wide, as ros HealthExpenditure's countries; the only example is data(OCC1950).

ftp1 to ftp4 are one indicator, 'searching for full time work at survey 1' to 4, of the same person's spell at four surveys as columns, one row per person, nobs counting the 'observations on the first spell', so the long form is person x survey, as Ecdat Griliches' paired years; duration and spell take one value per person, and the page fits no model.

quintile1 to p95 (Census Table F-1) and P90 to P99.99 (Piketty and Saez) are one measure, family income at a quantile, as columns, one row per Year, which the examples stack by percentile (reshape(..., idvar = 'Year', timevar = 'pctile', direction = 'long')) and fit lm(log(value/1000) ~ Year + variable*t1970p) on, so the long form is year x quantile, as HSAUR3 suicides2's age groups.

re74, re75 and re78 ('real earns., 1974' to '1978') and unem74, unem75 and unem78 are each man's earnings and unemployment in three years as columns, one row per man, as DAAG nswdemo (wide in this pass), whose men these are: the same 445 men as DAAG nsw74demo, with the same treatment, age, schooling, race, marriage, degree and earnings, a subset of nswdemo's 722, so the table leaves as its copy; the notes' analyses (Computer Exercise C17.8, a Tobit of re78 on train) fit no random effect.

re74, re75 and re78 and unem74, unem75 and unem78 are each man's earnings and unemployment in three years as columns, one row per man, as DAAG nswdemo (wide in this pass); its men are ros Lalonde/NSW_dw_obs.dta's 185 NSW trainees and 2,490 PSID comparison men with the same values ('a subset of that originally used by Lalonde'), so the table leaves as its copy, as camerondata nswproject and Ecdat Treatment did; the page fits no model.

emp232 and wage232 through emp056 and wage056 ('employment, sector 232, 1000s', 'hourly wage, sector 232, $') are two measures of eleven sectors as columns, with logs and growth rates of some, one row per month (t, 'linear time trend, 1 to 612'), so the sector is the unit stored wide, as zuur_mixed Ythan's species; the page fits no model.

Ee of Ne (ketotifen) and Ec of Nc (control) are each trial's children with treatment success and children in its two arms as columns ('number of children with treament success (ketotifen group)'), one row per trial; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and metabin(Ee, Ne, Ec, Nc, method = 'I') pools them with a blinding subgroup analysis; metadat holds no long form.

ep1t to ep6t of nt (high dose) and ep1c to ep6c of nc (standard dose) are each trial's events for six end points in its two arms as columns ('number of events in the high dose group for end point 1'), one row per trial; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and rma.mh(measure = 'OR', ai = ep1t, n1i = nt, ci = ep1c, n2i = nc) pools them; metadat holds no long form.

p2y12.mi to p2y12.vdeath of p2y12.total and aspirin.mi to aspirin.vdeath of aspirin.total are each study's events per end point in its two arms as columns ('number of patients with stroke in experimental group'), one row per study; binomial counts stack into the study x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and escalc(measure = 'OR') with rma.uni, metabin and bayesmeta pools them; metadat holds no long form.

bc.ins.ins, bc.ins.del and bc.del.del (cases) and ct.ins.ins, ct.ins.del and ct.del.del (controls) are each study's genotype counts in its two groups as columns ('number of cases who have a homozygous insertion polymorphism'), one row per study; the counts stack into the study x group long form, as dat.gibson2002's and HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and escalc(measure = 'OR') with rma pools them; metadat holds no long form.

ai of n1i (vaccinated) and ci of n2i (placebo) are each study's cholera cases and individuals in its two arms as columns ('number of cholera cases in the vaccinated group'), one row per study; binomial counts stack into the study x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and rma.mh(measure = 'RR') pools them; metadat holds no long form.

Ee of Ne (high-dose chemotherapy) and Ec of Nc (standard chemotherapy) are each trial's complete responses and patients in its two arms as columns, one row per trial; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and metabin(Ee, Ne, Ec, Nc) pools them; metadat holds no long form.

ai of n1i (reduced osmolarity solution) and ci of n2i (standard solution) are each trial's children requiring an unscheduled intravenous infusion and children in its two arms as columns, one row per trial; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and rma.mh(measure = 'OR') pools them; metadat holds no long form.

x.nrt of n.nrt (NRT) and x.ctrl of n.ctrl (control) are each comparison's abstinent participants and participants in its two arms as columns, one row per comparison, study repeating only for the two studies that test several NRT types (Piper 2009, Moolchan 2005); binomial counts stack into the study x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms and dat.anand1999's multiarm trials, and rma.mh(measure = 'RR') pools them per treatment and combined; metadat holds no long form.

resp.halo, fail.halo and miss.halo (haloperidol) and resp.plac, fail.plac and miss.plac (placebo) are each trial's responders, failures and missing observations in its two arms as columns, one row per trial; the counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and metabin with metamiss's imputation scenarios pools them; metadat holds no long form.

ai of n1i (lidocaine) and ci of n2i (control) are each study's deaths and patients in its two arms as columns, one row per study; binomial counts stack into the study x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and escalc(measure = 'RD') with rma pools them; metadat holds no long form.

y1i to y4i (with v1i to v4i) are each study's mean UPDRS differences at 3, 6 and 12 months and the long-term follow-up as columns ('the same patients were followed over time within a study'), one row per study; the page reshapes them long and fits rma.mv(yi, V, mods = ~ 0 + factor(time), random = ~ time | study, struct = 'HAR'), as dat.fine1993's, and metadat holds no long form.

Ee of Ne (pharmacotherapy) and Ec of Nc (control) are each study's fatal cerebrovascular events and patients in its two arms as columns, one row per study; binomial counts stack into the study x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and metabin(Ee, Ne, Ec, Nc, sm = 'OR', method = 'Peto') pools them; metadat holds no long form.

ihd.cont and noihd.cont (control) and ihd.exp and noihd.exp (treated) are each trial's ischaemic heart disease events and non-events in its two arms as columns, one row per trial, beside the OR, logOR and varlogOR computed from them; binomial counts stack into the trial x arm long form, as HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and metabin with metareg(m, cholr) pools them; metadat holds no long form.

non.pos and non.neg (non-circumcised) and cir.pos and cir.neg (circumcised) are each study's HIV positive and negative men in its two groups as columns, one row per study; the counts stack into the study x group long form, as dat.gibson2002's and HSAUR3 aspirin's arms, and escalc(measure = 'OR') with rma pools them, also by category; metadat holds no long form.

NCPRF.T1 to NCPRF.T3 are each team's newcomer performance at three time points as columns ('assessed newcomer performance over three additional time points'), one row per team (ID); the page's model, lme(MULTDV ~ NCEMP*TIME + TMEXP*TIME + TMPRF*TIME, random = ~TIME|ID), runs on the make.univ stack, and multilevel holds no long form.

read1 to read6 (with age1 to age6) are each pupil's reading score at six occasions as columns ('Reading score data for 407 pupils across 6 occasions'), one row per pupil (id); demo(UserGuide13) reshapes them long and fits runMLwiN(reading ~ 1 + (1 | student) + (1 | occasion)), and R2MLwiN holds no long form.

NSW, Vic, Qld, SA, WA, Tas, NT and ACT are one measure, the 'population counts' of eight states and territories, as columns beside their total Aust, one row per year (1917, 1927, ..., 1997), so the long form is year x state, as DAAG jobs' regions; the examples compute each state's growth rate and plot its population, no model.

seAVt to ausAVt (temperature) and seRain to ausRain (rainfall) are two measures of the same regions as columns ('area-weighted averages for the respective regions'), one row per Year, so the long form is year x region, as DAAG jobs' regions; the shared page plots only bomregions2021, and this table is no copy of bomregions2021, whose temperatures and rainfall differ in nearly every common year (bomregions left as this table's copy).

seAVt to ausAVt (temperature) and seRain to ausRain (rainfall) are two measures of the same regions as columns ('area-weighted averages for the respective regions'), one row per Year, so the long form is year x region, as DAAG jobs' regions; Maindonald, Braun and Andrews (2024, ch3.qmd) fit lqs(northRain ~ SOI + CO2), a resistant regression of one region's series, no random effect.

Jan to Dec are one measure, the 'average January SOI values for each year' to December, in one column per month, one row per Year, as agridat vargas.txe.covs' monthly weather, and NTrain to swRain one rainfall measure of six regions; the examples fit arima(detrendRain, xreg = detrendSOI) on the annual avrain and SOI, no random effect.

Lab and IA400 are one measure, the sugar concentration of each 25 g sample 'as measured by 2 methods', as columns, one row per sample, so the long form is sample x method, as DAAG ironslag's; Maindonald, Braun and Andrews (2024, ch6.qmd) fit auto.arima(IA400, xreg = Lab), no random effect.

mbac, mpl, fbac and fpl are the average reductions in VAS pain rating of four groups of different patients, males and females with and without baclofen (avbac and avplac their averages), at nine times ('every 20 minutes, from 10 minutes to 170 minutes'), one row per time (min): group means of a fixed sex by treatment design rather than observations, as HSAUR3 toothpaste's arm means, so no unit repeats; the page only plots them and weights them by the group sizes, and Maindonald, Braun and Andrews (2024, ch3.qmd) stack minute 30 alone to show that weighting.

Erie, michHuron, Ontario and StClair are one measure, the yearly average height, of four lakes as columns ('stored as a multivariate time series'), one row per year 1918-2009, so the long form is year x lake, as DAAG jobs' regions; the only example plots it.

cross and self are the heights of each pair's crossed and self-fertilized plant ('Plants were paired within the pots in which they were grown') as columns, one row per pair, so the long form is pair x fertilization, as DAAG pair65's bands; the pots ('5 pots, holding 5,5,5,5,4 pairs', Maindonald, Braun and Andrews 2024, ch2.qmd) are no column, and the examples compare cross - self.

four and one are each panelist's sweetness assessments of two milk samples ('Each of 17 panelists compared two milk samples for sweetness') as columns, one row per panelist, so the long form is panelist x sample, as HSAUR3 students' two forms; the example plots four ~ one.

heated and ambient are the stretch of each pair's two bands ('Eighteen elastic bands were divided into nine pairs', one member of each heated) as columns, one row per pair, so the long form is pair x treatment, as wooldridge audit's tester pairs; the examples take the mean and sd of heated - ambient.

window1, window2 and window3 are one measure, the object shown, in each of a play's three windows as columns ('At each play, each of three windows shows one of 7 possible objects'), one row per play, which the example stacks (stack(vlt[,1:3])), so the long form is play x window, as carData DavisThin's items; prize follows from the three objects and night has two levels.

LAT and LONG identify the collection sites of the '948 accessions from European Arabidopsis thaliana populations', 135 of the 477 distinct locations holding 2 to 75 accessions over which the climatic variables are constant, and the example's fitme(cbind(pos1046738,1-pos1046738) ~ seasonal + Matern(1|LAT+LONG), family = binomial(), method = 'PQL/L') gives each distinct location one value of its Matern random effect, so LAT:LONG is a grouping factor, as pymc_examples gambia_dataset's x:y; re-filed with LAT:LONG.

Strain indexes the 213 bacterial strains whose spectra repeat within them (571 rows), BeyondArena's group_on with group_labels 'per_group' ('replicate a grouped-based task to predict the species of strains'), but Species is constant within every strain, so the one-label rule keeps its filing; the table is not cached on this laptop, so the counts are the filing line's and the help page's.

code_module indexes the seven modules whose presentations repeat within it (two to four of code_presentation's four each), one row per module presentation with its module_presentation_length, the lookup that studentInfo.csv and the other OULAD files join on, with no outcome, so it stays excluded by the lookup rule, as uci_349 assessments.csv and vle.csv.

One row per observation of y ('dependent variable'), x ('regressor variable') and z ('instrument variable'), no column indexing a unit, and the page fits ivreg(y ~ x | z) without grouping; the title calls the data artificial ('Artificial Weak Instrument Data', 'Artificial data set to illustrate the problem of weak instruments'), so it leaves as simulated data.

goldstandard, perfect.cor, noise, location and scale are one quantity of each sample by the gold standard and four new methods as columns ('Data to compare a new method against a gold standard'), one row per sample, so the long form is sample x method, as DAAG ironslag's two methods; Lazic's chapter 5 code (stanlazic.github.io/EDLB_Rcode/Ch5_Planning.txt) only plots each against goldstandard and compares them by cor() and lin.cor(). The page calls the data simulated ('Simulated data for one gold standard and four other outcome variables'), so it leaves as simulated data.
